claims.claim: Stalling during the synthesis of the FLAG-His3 fusion protein in the two stalling reporters leads to degradation of the nascent peptide.
claims.source: Finally, stalling during the synthesis of the FLAG-His3 fusion protein in the two stalling reporters (NGD-CGA and NGD-AAA) leads to degradation of the nascent peptide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, FLAG panel).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: CUE2 overexpression was the strongest outlier by Z-score causing reduced GFP expression for both NGD reporters, without affecting the OPT reporter.
claims.source: By far, the strongest outlier by Z-score causing reduced GFP expression for both NGD reporters, without affecting the OPT reporter, resulted from overexpression of the gene CUE2 (Figure 1C–1D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the overexpression screen data shown in Figure 1C-1D.

claims.claim: NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels are substantially reduced upon CUE2 overexpression whereas the control RFP transcript is not affected.
claims.source: Flow cytometry and northern analysis confirm that NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels are substantially reduced upon CUE2 overexpression whereas the control RFP transcript is not affected (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and northern blot data in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Cue2 contains two conserved CUE ubiquitin-binding domains at the N-terminus.
claims.source: Cue2 contains two conserved CUE (coupling of ubiquitin to ER degradation) ubiquitin-binding domains at the N-terminus (Kang et al., 2003), followed by two putative ubiquitin-binding domains (UBA* (ubiquitin-associated domain) and CUE* domain, respectively), and an SMR (small MutS-related) hydrolase domain at the C-terminus (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by domain analysis and citation to previous work, as shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Cue2 contains an SMR (small MutS-related) hydrolase domain at the C-terminus.
claims.source: Cue2 contains two conserved CUE (coupling of ubiquitin to ER degradation) ubiquitin-binding domains at the N-terminus (Kang et al., 2003), followed by two putative ubiquitin-binding domains (UBA* (ubiquitin-associated domain) and CUE* domain, respectively), and an SMR (small MutS-related) hydrolase domain at the C-terminus (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by domain analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The human NEDD4-binding protein 2, N4BP2, is a putative homolog of Cue2.
claims.source: We performed alignments of the CUE and SMR domains of Cue2 using structure-based alignment tools (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and found putative homologs in various kingdoms of life, including the human NEDD4-binding protein 2, N4BP2.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structure-based alignment data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claims.claim: The SMR domain of SOT1 in plants exhibits RNA endonuclease activity.
claims.source: While the SMR domain of MutS family enzymes canonically functions as a DNA-nicking hydrolase (Fukui and Kuramitsu, 2011), the SMR domain of SOT1 in plants exhibits RNA endonuclease activity (Zhou et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: SMR domains show structural similarity to bacterial RNase E.
claims.source: Additionally, SMR domains show structural similarity to bacterial RNase E (Fukui and Kuramitsu, 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 in Cue2 are positioned along the mRNA channel in the homology model.
claims.source: We aligned the Cue2-SMR homology model with the structure of the IF3-CTD on the ribosome and observed that conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 are positioned along the mRNA channel in this model (Figure 2C–2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E–F) and thus represent potential residues critical for endonucleolytic cleavage activity; additionally, R402 had previously been implicated in the RNA cleavage activity of other SMR domains (Zhou et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by homology modeling shown in Figure 2C-2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-F.

claims.claim: R402 had previously been implicated in the RNA cleavage activity of other SMR domains.
claims.source: We aligned the Cue2-SMR homology model with the structure of the IF3-CTD on the ribosome and observed that conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 are positioned along the mRNA channel in this model (Figure 2C–2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E–F) and thus represent potential residues critical for endonucleolytic cleavage activity; additionally, R402 had previously been implicated in the RNA cleavage activity of other SMR domains (Zhou et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Individually mutating the conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 to alanine causes a modest increase in GFP expression relative to CUE2 WT.
claims.source: We find that individually mutating the conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 to alanine (A) causes a modest increase in GFP expression relative to CUE2 WT, whereas the R402K mutation (which maintains a positively charged amino acid) has no discernible effect (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: The R402K mutation has no discernible effect on GFP expression.
claims.source: We find that individually mutating the conserved residues D348, H350, and R402 to alanine (A) causes a modest increase in GFP expression relative to CUE2 WT, whereas the R402K mutation (which maintains a positively charged amino acid) has no discernible effect (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Mutating residues 348 through 350 nearly restores GFP reporter signal.
claims.source: Mutating residues 348 through 350, which includes the conserved residues D348 and H350, nearly restores GFP reporter signal in this assay (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Deletion of CUE2 in the ski2Δ background causes both 5' and 3' decay intermediates to disappear.
claims.source: Upon deletion of CUE2 in the appropriate yeast background, we see that both of these decay intermediates disappear (Figure 2F; lane 2 and Figure 2G; lane 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2F and 2G.

claims.claim: Deletion of the C-terminal portion of CUE2 comprising the SMR domain results in a complete loss of endonucleolytic cleavage.
claims.source: As a first test, we deleted the C-terminal portion of CUE2 comprising the SMR domain and revealed a complete loss of endonucleolytic cleavage (Figure 2H, lane 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: Combined mutations in CUE2 at D348 and H350 result in a complete abolishment of endonucleolytic cleavage activity.
claims.source: To further refine this analysis, we made combined mutations in CUE2 at D348 and H350 and observed a complete abolishment of endonucleolytic cleavage activity (Figure 2H, lane 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: Deletion of CUE2 in the WT, ski2Δ or xrn1Δ background does not demonstrably impact GFP or steady-state full-length mRNA levels.
claims.source: Surprisingly, deletion of CUE2 in the WT, ski2Δ or xrn1Δ background does not demonstrably impact GFP or steady-state full-length mRNA levels (Figure 3A–3B, Figure 2F, or Figure 2G, respectively) suggesting that the endonucleolytic decay pathway is not responsible for the majority of the three-fold loss in mRNA levels observed for this NGD reporter (relative to OPT, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A-3B, Figure 2F, and Figure 2G.

claims.claim: Deleting XRN1 alone greatly restores NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels.
claims.source: However, we see that deleting XRN1 alone greatly restores NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels while deleting SKI2 alone has very little effect (Figure 3A–3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 3A-3B.

claims.claim: Deleting SKI2 alone has very little effect on NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels.
claims.source: However, we see that deleting XRN1 alone greatly restores NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels while deleting SKI2 alone has very little effect (Figure 3A–3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 3A-3B.

claims.claim: The majority of mRNA degradation observed for the NGD-CGA reporter is mediated by canonical decay pathways, mostly through Xrn1.
claims.source: These results together suggest that the majority of mRNA degradation observed for the NGD-CGA reporter is mediated by canonical decay pathways, mostly through Xrn1.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the northern blot data showing that XRN1 deletion restores mRNA levels.

claims.claim: In the ski2Δ slh1Δ and xrn1Δ slh1Δ strains, there is a sizeable build-up of endonucleolytically cleaved mRNA fragments.
claims.source: We found that in the ski2Δ slh1Δ and xrn1Δ slh1Δ strains, we see a sizeable build-up of endonucleolytically cleaved mRNA fragments (Figure 2F; lane 3 and Figure 2G; lane 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2F and 2G.

claims.claim: In the absence of SLH1, there is smearing of the signal representative of shorter 5' and longer 3' fragments due to additional cleavage events occurring upstream of the primary stall site.
claims.source: Consistent with the recent study by Ikeuchi et al. (2019), we also see smearing of the signal representative of shorter 5' and longer 3' fragments due to additional cleavage events occurring upstream of the primary stall site in the absence of SLH1.
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: A robust decrease in full-length mRNA levels is observed upon deletion of SLH1.
claims.source: Importantly, we also observe a robust decrease in full-length mRNA levels upon deletion of SLH1 (Figure 2F; lane 3 and Figure 2G; lane 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2F and 2G.

claims.claim: Slh1 activity competes with Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic cleavage.
claims.source: These data suggest a model wherein Slh1 activity somehow competes with Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic cleavage.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that deletion of SLH1 increases Cue2-mediated cleavage.

claims.claim: Deletion of CUE2 in the xrn1Δ slh1Δ background results in a complete loss of the decay intermediate and a restoration of full-length mRNA levels.
claims.source: To ask whether the increased endonucleolytic cleavage seen in the SLH1 deletion background is the result of Cue2 activity, we deleted CUE2 in the xrn1Δ slh1Δ background and observed a complete loss of the decay intermediate and a restoration of full-length mRNA levels (Figure 2G; lane 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2G.

claims.claim: The action of Slh1 negatively regulates the assembly of a potent Cue2 substrate.
claims.source: These data provide strong evidence that the action of Slh1 negatively regulates the assembly of a potent Cue2 substrate though the molecular mechanism for this regulation is not defined.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing increased Cue2 activity in slh1Δ backgrounds.

claims.claim: 16 nucleotide RPFs correspond to ribosomes that have translated to the truncated end of an mRNA in the cell.
claims.source: 16 nucleotide (nt) RPFs correspond to ribosomes that have translated to the truncated end of an mRNA in the cell, usually an mRNA that has been endonucleolytically processed; these 16 nt RFPs are enriched in a dom34Δ strain since these are established targets for Dom34-mediated ribosome rescue (Arribere and Fire, 2018; Guydosh and Green, 2017; Guydosh and Green, 2014; Guydosh et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work establishing this interpretation.

claims.claim: 16 nt RPFs are enriched in a dom34Δ strain since these are established targets for Dom34-mediated ribosome rescue.
claims.source: 16 nucleotide (nt) RPFs correspond to ribosomes that have translated to the truncated end of an mRNA in the cell, usually an mRNA that has been endonucleolytically processed; these 16 nt RFPs are enriched in a dom34Δ strain since these are established targets for Dom34-mediated ribosome rescue (Arribere and Fire, 2018; Guydosh and Green, 2017; Guydosh and Green, 2014; Guydosh et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: 21 and 28 nt RPFs are derived from ribosomes on intact mRNA, with the two sizes corresponding to different conformational states of ribosomes in the elongation cycle.
claims.source: 21 and 28 nt RPFs are derived from ribosomes on intact mRNA, with the two sizes corresponding to different conformational states of ribosomes in the elongation cycle (Lareau et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2019b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: 21 nt RPFs represent classical/decoding ribosomes waiting for the next aminoacyl-tRNA.
claims.source: In our modified ribosome profiling library preparation (Wu et al., 2019b) 21 nt RPFs represent classical/decoding ribosomes waiting for the next aminoacyl-tRNA whereas the 28 nt RPFs primarily represent ribosomes in a rotated/pre-translocation state.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to the modified ribosome profiling method.

claims.claim: 28 nt RPFs primarily represent ribosomes in a rotated/pre-translocation state.
claims.source: In our modified ribosome profiling library preparation (Wu et al., 2019b) 21 nt RPFs represent classical/decoding ribosomes waiting for the next aminoacyl-tRNA whereas the 28 nt RPFs primarily represent ribosomes in a rotated/pre-translocation state.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to the modified ribosome profiling method.

claims.claim: Deleting SKI2 generally stabilizes prematurely polyadenylated and truncated mRNAs in the cell.
claims.source: We note that deleting SKI2 generally stabilizes prematurely polyadenylated and truncated mRNAs in the cell, as seen previously (Tsuboi et al., 2012; van Hoof et al., 2002); therefore, use of this background likely enhanced Cue2 cleavage on these mRNA substrates.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: In ski2Δ, there is a clear accumulation of ribosome density at the (CGA)12 stall site in the 21 nt RPF track.
claims.source: In ski2Δ, we observe a clear accumulation of ribosome density at the (CGA)12 stall site (in the 21 nt RPF track) in our reporter (Figure 4A) consistent with ribosome stalling at this site.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: A quadruplet of 21 nt RPF peaks is observed from the second to the fifth CGA codon within the (CGA)12 codon tract.
claims.source: Looking first within the actual (CGA)12 codon tract, we see a quadruplet of 21 nt RPF peaks from the second to the fifth CGA codon (Figure 4A, middle panel).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The principal ribosome accumulation occurs between the second and the fifth CGA codon.
claims.source: Because of difficulties in mapping monosome reads to repetitive sequences such as (CGA)12, we also isolated longer RPFs from a minor (<5% of total reads on reporter) population of stacked disome species (Guydosh and Green, 2014) and show that although some ribosomes move into the subsequent CGA codons, the principal ribosome accumulation occurs between the second and the fifth codon (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by disome footprint data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Most ribosomes found at the CGA codons are waiting to decode the next aminoacyl-tRNA.
claims.source: While 21 nt RFPs are enriched on CGA codons, 28 nt RPFs are not (Figure 4A, compare middle and bottom panels), indicating that most ribosomes found at the CGA codons are waiting to decode the next aminoacyl-tRNA; these observations are consistent with the fact that CGA codons are poorly decoded (Letzring et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4A and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The 21 nt RPF quadruplet at the CGA cluster represents the stalled 'lead' ribosome in its classical (unrotated) conformation.
claims.source: The 21 nt RPF quadruplet at the CGA cluster represents the stalled 'lead' ribosome in its classical (unrotated) conformation, which is consistent with recent cryo-EM structures of collided ribosomes (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on ribosome profiling data and supported by citations to cryo-EM structures.

claims.claim: About 30 nts upstream of the lead ribosomes, there is accumulation of 28 nt RPFs that correspond to colliding ribosomes in a rotated state.
claims.source: About 30 nts upstream of these lead ribosomes, we observe the accumulation of 28 nt RPFs that correspond to colliding ribosomes in a rotated state (Figure 4A, bottom panel), also in agreement with the ribosome states recently reported in cryo-EM structures of collided disomes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4A and is consistent with cryo-EM structures.

claims.claim: In the dom34Δ ski2Δ strain, a strong quadruplet of 16 nt RPF peaks is observed exactly 30 nts upstream of the quadruplet of 21 nt RPFs.
claims.source: In the dom34Δ ski2Δ strain (where 16 nt RPFs are stabilized), we observe a strong quadruplet of 16 nt RPF peaks exactly 30 nts upstream of the quadruplet of 21 nt RPFs (Figure 4B), indicative of endonucleolytic cleavage events occurring upstream of the (CGA)12–stalled ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: The precise 30 nt distance between the 16 nt RPFs and the downstream 21 nt RPFs is consistent with the measured distance between the A sites of two colliding ribosomes.
claims.source: The precise 30 nt distance between the 16 nt RPFs and the downstream 21 nt RPFs is consistent with the measured distance between the A sites of two colliding ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the ribosome profiling data and knowledge of ribosome structure.

claims.claim: In the cue2Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ strain, the 16 nt RPFs indicative of endonucleolytic cleavage are dramatically reduced in abundance.
claims.source: To address the role of Cue2 as the endonuclease, we examined the same collection of RPFs in the cue2Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ strain. In this background, the 16 nt RPFs indicative of endonucleolytic cleavage are dramatically reduced in abundance while the distributions of 21 and 28 nt RPFs are largely unaffected (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Endonucleolytic cleavage occurs precisely in the A site of the collided, rotated ribosome and requires Cue2.
claims.source: These data argue that endonucleolytic cleavage occurs precisely in the A site of the collided, rotated ribosome and requires Cue2.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the ribosome profiling data showing loss of 16 nt RPFs in cue2Δ.

claims.claim: In the slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ strain, there is a dramatic accumulation of 16 nt RPF peaks behind the lead ribosomes.
claims.source: When we delete DOM34 in the slh1Δ ski2Δ background (slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ), we see a dramatic accumulation of 16 nt RPF peaks (again, as a quadruplet, although with an altered relative distribution) behind the lead ribosomes (Figure 4E compared to 4B, top panels, note the larger y-axis scale in Figure 4E and 4F compared to 4B and 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Deletion of CUE2 in the slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ background leads to a near complete loss of the 16 nt RPFs.
claims.source: Importantly, deletion of CUE2 in the slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ background leads to a near complete loss of the 16 nt RPFs (Figure 4F, top panel) and an enrichment of 21 and 28 nt RPFs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Endonucleolytic cleavage events associated with NGD depend on the E3 ligase Hel2.
claims.source: Lastly, consistent with earlier studies showing that endonucleolytic cleavage events associated with NGD depend on the E3 ligase Hel2 (Ikeuchi et al., 2019), we show that deletion of HEL2 in both dom34Δ ski2Δ and slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ backgrounds leads to a complete loss of 16 nt RPFs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and f, respectively).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: On addition of Cue2-SMR (WT), there is a substantial loss of trisomes and a corresponding increase in monosomes and disomes.
claims.source: Nevertheless, on addition of Cue2-SMR (WT) (pink trace), we observe a substantial loss of trisomes and a corresponding increase in monosomes and disomes (Figure 5A), while on addition of the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant (orange trace), we observe a more modest decrease in trisomes (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by sucrose gradient data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: On addition of the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant, there is a more modest decrease in trisomes.
claims.source: Nevertheless, on addition of Cue2-SMR (WT) (pink trace), we observe a substantial loss of trisomes and a corresponding increase in monosomes and disomes (Figure 5A), while on addition of the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant (orange trace), we observe a more modest decrease in trisomes (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by sucrose gradient data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: The SMR (hydrolase) domain of Cue2 cleaves the mRNA within a stack of colliding ribosomes in vitro.
claims.source: These results provide initial in vitro evidence that the SMR (hydrolase) domain of Cue2 cleaves the mRNA within a stack of colliding ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the in vitro cleavage assay data.

claims.claim: In the sample treated with the wild-type Cue2-SMR domain, there is a striking accumulation of 3' fragment ends that maps precisely where the strong cleavage sites were reported in the ribosome profiling data.
claims.source: In the sample treated with the wild-type Cue2-SMR domain, we see a striking accumulation of 3' fragment ends that maps precisely where the strong cleavage sites were reported (in the A site of the colliding ribosome) in the ribosome profiling data for the same strain (slh1Δ dom34Δ sk2iΔ); reassuringly, these cleavage events are not seen in the sequencing data for the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant or for the no enzyme control (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The cleavage events are not seen in the sequencing data for the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant or for the no enzyme control.
claims.source: In the sample treated with the wild-type Cue2-SMR domain, we see a striking accumulation of 3' fragment ends that maps precisely where the strong cleavage sites were reported (in the A site of the colliding ribosome) in the ribosome profiling data for the same strain (slh1Δ dom34Δ sk2iΔ); reassuringly, these cleavage events are not seen in the sequencing data for the Cue2 SMR-R402A mutant or for the no enzyme control (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The remarkable agreement between the in vivo-based ribosome profiling data and the in vitro-based cleavage data provides strong support for the identity of Cue2 as the endonuclease involved in NGD.
claims.source: The remarkable agreement between the in vivo-based ribosome profiling data and the in vitro-based cleavage data provides strong support for the identity of Cue2 as the endonuclease involved in NGD.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the concordance of in vivo and in vitro data.

claims.claim: When SLH1 is deleted, there is a substantial build-up of RPFs both at the stalling site (21 nt RPFs) and upstream (28 nt RPFs) of the stalling site.
claims.source: However, when we compared RPFs on the uncleaved mRNAs (i.e. the 21 and 28 nt RPFs) in the cue2Δ dom34Δ ski2∆ and slh1Δ cue2Δ dom34Δ ski2∆ strains, we observed that SLH1 deletion results in a substantial build-up of RPFs both at the stalling site (21 nt RPFs) (compare middle panels, Figure 4C and 4F) and upstream (28 nt RPFs) of the stalling site (compare bottom panels, Figure 4C and 4F and quantitation in 4H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4C, 4F, and 4H.

claims.claim: SLH1 deletion results in more than a twofold increase in ribosome occupancy.
claims.source: These data were normalized to overall mRNA levels and reveal more than a twofold increase in ribosome occupancy when SLH1 is deleted.
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitation of ribosome profiling data.

claims.claim: Slh1 prevents the accumulation of colliding ribosomes.
claims.source: These data are consistent with the proposed model that Slh1 prevents the accumulation of colliding ribosomes (Matsuo et al., 2017) thereby limiting the availability of Cue2 substrates.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on ribosome profiling data and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs are one possible endogenous target class for Cue2.
claims.source: One possible endogenous target class for Cue2 is the set of prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs (where polyadenylation happens within the ORF) that are commonly generated by aberrant RNA processing events in the nucleus.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the known properties of these mRNAs.

claims.claim: Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs are substantially enriched in the prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs.
claims.source: We next identify Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs in a ski2∆ dom34∆ strain (Figure 6A, orange dots) as well as in a ski2∆ dom34∆ slh1∆ background (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, orange dots) and see that they are substantially enriched in the prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, red dots).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: In the ski2∆ dom34∆ background, a good fraction (21/55) of the prematurely polyadenylated genes are substantially reduced in 16 nt RPFs upon CUE2 deletion.
claims.source: We note that in the ski2∆ dom34∆ background a good fraction (21/55) of the prematurely polyadenylated genes are substantially reduced in 16 nt RPFs upon CUE2 deletion (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: For well-defined mRNA targets RNA14 and YAP1, the Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs are positioned directly upstream of the previously characterized sites of premature polyadenylation.
claims.source: Moreover, we show that for well-defined mRNA targets RNA14 and YAP1, the Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs are positioned as anticipated directly upstream of the previously characterized sites of premature polyadenylation (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C) (Guydosh and Green, 2017; Pelechano et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Cue2-cleavage may be one mechanism for cells to initiate decay of prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs.
claims.source: Although the SKI complex and the exosome decay NSD substrates (Frischmeyer et al., 2002; van Hoof et al., 2002), Cue2-cleavage may be one mechanism for cells to initiate this decay.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the data showing Cue2 activity on prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs.

claims.claim: The ubiquitin-binding domains of Cue2 might recognize Hel2-ubiquitinated sites on the stacked ribosomes thus allowing recruitment of the SMR domain into the A site of the colliding ribosome.
claims.source: We suspect that the ubiquitin-binding domains of Cue2 might recognize Hel2-ubiquitinated sites on the stacked ribosomes thus allowing recruitment of the SMR domain into the A site of the colliding ribosome.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the domain structure of Cue2 and the known role of Hel2.

claims.claim: Recognition of ubiquitin chains by Cue2 might involve multiple ubiquitinated sites on a single collided ribosome or those found on neighboring ribosomes.
claims.source: We can imagine that recognition of ubiquitin chains by Cue2 might involve multiple ubiquitinated sites on a single collided ribosome or those found on neighboring ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of Cue2 recruitment.

claims.claim: The conserved and putative ubiquitin-binding domains might function within Cue2 itself to inhibit promiscuous activity of the endonuclease in the absence of an appropriate target.
claims.source: These conserved and putative ubiquitin-binding domains might also function within Cue2 itself to inhibit promiscuous activity of the endonuclease in the absence of an appropriate target, a possibility that prompted us to perform in vitro cleavage experiments with the isolated SMR domain of Cue2.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the regulatory function of the ubiquitin-binding domains.

claims.claim: Canonical exonucleolytic processing of problematic mRNAs is the dominant pathway on the NGD-CGA reporter, with the strongest contributions from Xrn1 rather than the exosome.
claims.source: We show that canonical exonucleolytic processing of problematic mRNAs is the dominant pathway on our NGD-CGA reporter, with the strongest contributions from Xrn1 rather than the exosome (Figure 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: The Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic pathway is activated in genetic backgrounds lacking the helicase Slh1.
claims.source: Importantly, we find that the Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic pathway is activated in genetic backgrounds lacking the helicase Slh1 (a member of the previously identified RQT complex) (Figure 2F–2G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2F-2G.

claims.claim: Under conditions where cells are overwhelmed by colliding ribosome complexes, the RQT machinery might become limiting and there will be an increased role for Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic processing.
claims.source: Our genetic insights also lead us to speculate that under conditions where cells are overwhelmed by colliding ribosome complexes, for example under stressful RNA-damaging conditions (Simms et al., 2014), that the RQT machinery might become limiting and that there will be an increased role for Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic processing.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the genetic data and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Previous genetic screens reveal increased sensitivity of CUE2 deletion strains to ribosome-targeted compounds.
claims.source: Previous genetic screens reveal increased sensitivity of CUE2 deletion strains to ribosome-targeted compounds (Alamgir et al., 2010; Mircus et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: The strong conservation of Cue2 throughout eukaryotes argues that this endonucleolytic processing pathway plays a fundamental role in biology.
claims.source: More generally, the strong conservation of Cue2 throughout eukaryotes argues that this endonucleolytic processing pathway plays a fundamental role in biology.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of conservation.

claims.claim: The activity of the RQT complex is critical in targeting nascent peptides on problematic mRNAs for degradation via the RQC.
claims.source: Previous studies provide strong evidence that the activity of the RQT complex is critical in targeting nascent peptides on problematic mRNAs for degradation via the RQC (Matsuo et al., 2017; Sitron et al., 2017) through ribosome rescue events that generate a dissociated 60S-peptidyl-tRNA complex.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Ribosome occupancies on problematic mRNAs increase on deletion of SLH1.
claims.source: Our ribosome profiling results indicate that ribosome occupancies on problematic mRNAs increase on deletion of SLH1 (Figure 4C, 4F and 4H) consistent with the possibility that Slh1 functions directly or indirectly to dissociate ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 4C, 4F, and 4H.

claims.claim: The increased Cue2-dependent cleavage observed in slh1∆ background suggests that an increase in the density of collided ribosomes makes an ideal Cue2 substrate.
claims.source: The increased Cue2-dependent cleavage (Figure 2F–2G and Figure 4B and 4E) that we observe in slh1∆ background suggests that an increase in the density of collided ribosomes makes an ideal Cue2 substrate.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing increased cleavage in slh1∆.

claims.claim: Slh1 and Dom34 may both target collided ribosomes for the RQC, although their specificities may be somewhat distinct.
claims.source: Taken together, we suggest that Slh1 and Dom34 may both target collided ribosomes for the RQC, although their specificities may be somewhat distinct.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the data presented.

claims.claim: Slh1 may use its helicase function to target ribosomes on intact mRNAs with an accessible 3' end, while Dom34 targets those ribosomes on truncated mRNAs that are inaccessible to Slh1 activity.
claims.source: For example, Slh1 may use its helicase function to target ribosomes on intact mRNAs with an accessible 3' end, while Dom34 targets those ribosomes on truncated mRNAs that are inaccessible to Slh1 activity.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the distinct roles of Slh1 and Dom34.

claims.claim: A critical role of Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic cleavage is to provide another pathway for ribosome dissociation that can target nascent peptides for RQC.
claims.source: In this view, a critical role of Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic cleavage is to provide another pathway for ribosome dissociation that can target nascent peptides for RQC.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the role of Cue2 in the broader quality control pathway.

claims.claim: Dom34 preferentially rescues ribosomes that are trapped on truncated mRNAs.
claims.source: Previous studies provide strong support for the idea that Dom34 preferentially rescues ribosomes that are trapped on truncated mRNAs (Guydosh and Green, 2014; Shoemaker et al., 2010) and in vitro studies have connected this rescue activity of Dom34 to downstream RQC functions (Shao et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Two distinct rescue pathways exist: one on intact mRNA by the RQT complex (and Slh1) and the other on endonucleolytically cleaved mRNA by Dom34.
claims.source: These two distinct rescue pathways, one on intact mRNA by the RQT complex (and Slh1) and the other on endonucleolytically cleaved mRNA by Dom34, might provide the cell with redundant means to deal with toxic mRNP intermediates.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the data and previous work.

claims.claim: Proteotoxic stress is a critical problem for all cells and elaborate quality control systems have evolved to minimize its effects.
claims.source: Proteotoxic stress is a critical problem for all cells and elaborate quality control systems have evolved to minimize its effects as made clear by the exquisite sensitivity of neurons to defects in these pathways (Bengtson and Joazeiro, 2010; Ishimura et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and established knowledge.

claims.claim: The synergistic contributions of exonucleases and endonucleases for targeting problematic mRNAs for decay are critical for ensuring that proteotoxic stress is minimized.
claims.source: The synergistic contributions of exonucleases and endonucleases that we delineate here for targeting problematic mRNAs for decay are critical for ensuring that proteotoxic stress is minimized.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the data presented in the study.

results.result: Cue2 is identified as the conserved endonuclease responsible for NGD through a reverse genetic screen, and its SMR domain contains conserved residues (D348, H350, R402) critical for endonucleolytic cleavage activity.
results.evaluation: The identification of Cue2 through the overexpression screen (C28, C29) is well-supported by flow cytometry and northern blot data. The domain structure analysis (C30-C32, C35-C36) is supported by homology modeling and sequence alignments. Mutagenesis experiments (C37-C39, C41-C42) and deletion of CUE2 abolishing decay intermediates (C40) provide strong functional evidence. The convergence of genetic, structural, and biochemical data robustly supports this result.

results.result: Ribosome profiling reveals that Cue2 cleaves mRNA precisely in the A site of the colliding ribosome, positioned 30 nucleotides upstream of the stalled lead ribosome.
results.evaluation: The ribosome profiling data (C59-C67) provides high-resolution evidence for the precise cleavage site. The 16 nt RPFs appear exactly 30 nts upstream of the 21 nt RPFs marking the stalled ribosome (C65-C66), and these 16 nt RPFs are dramatically reduced in cue2Δ strains (C67). The spatial relationship between different RPF sizes and their interpretation as different ribosome states is well-supported by citations to previous work and is consistent with cryo-EM structures (C63-C64). This result is strongly supported.

results.result: NGD primarily proceeds via Xrn1-mediated exonucleolytic decay, with Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic decay constituting a secondary pathway under normal conditions.
results.evaluation: Northern blot data clearly shows that XRN1 deletion greatly restores NGD-CGA reporter mRNA levels (C44), while CUE2 deletion alone has minimal effect (C43). SKI2 deletion also has little effect (C45), indicating the exosome is not the primary pathway. The inference that Xrn1 mediates the majority of decay (C46) is well-supported by these data. This hierarchy of decay pathways is convincingly demonstrated.

results.result: The Cue2-dependent endonucleolytic pathway becomes a major contributor to NGD in cells lacking Slh1, which normally prevents accumulation of colliding ribosomes.
results.evaluation: Multiple lines of evidence support this result: northern blots show increased endonucleolytic cleavage fragments in slh1Δ backgrounds (C47-C49), deletion of CUE2 in slh1Δ backgrounds eliminates these fragments and restores full-length mRNA (C51), and ribosome profiling shows dramatic accumulation of 16 nt RPFs in slh1Δ dom34Δ ski2Δ that are lost upon CUE2 deletion (C69-C70). The increased ribosome occupancy in slh1Δ strains (C78-C79) provides a mechanistic explanation. The data converge to support the model that Slh1 negatively regulates Cue2 substrate formation.

results.result: In vitro reconstitution experiments demonstrate that the SMR domain of Cue2 is sufficient to cleave mRNA within colliding ribosomes, with cleavage sites matching those observed in vivo.
results.evaluation: The in vitro cleavage assays show that addition of wild-type Cue2-SMR causes substantial loss of trisomes (C72), while the R402A mutant has reduced activity (C73). RNA-seq of the in vitro cleavage products shows striking accumulation of 3' fragment ends that precisely match the in vivo cleavage sites (C75), and these are absent in the R402A mutant and no-enzyme controls (C76). The concordance between in vivo and in vitro data (C77) strongly supports the conclusion that Cue2-SMR is sufficient for cleavage activity.

results.result: Endonucleolytic cleavage events associated with NGD depend on the E3 ligase Hel2.
results.evaluation: Ribosome profiling data shows complete loss of 16 nt RPFs in hel2Δ backgrounds (C71), consistent with previous work. This result is well-supported by the data presented and citations to prior studies, though it represents confirmation of previous findings rather than a novel discovery in this manuscript.

results.result: Prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs are endogenous targets for Cue2-mediated cleavage, with Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs enriched at sites upstream of premature polyadenylation.
results.evaluation: The ribosome profiling data shows substantial enrichment of Cue2-dependent 16 nt RPFs in prematurely polyadenylated mRNAs (C82), with 21/55 genes showing substantial reduction in 16 nt RPFs upon CUE2 deletion (C83). For specific targets RNA14 and YAP1, the 16 nt RPFs are positioned precisely upstream of known premature polyadenylation sites (C84). While the functional significance is somewhat speculative (C85), the data clearly demonstrate that these mRNAs are Cue2 substrates.

results.result: The NGD-CGA and NGD-AAA reporters exhibit robust decreases in GFP/RFP ratios compared to the OPT control, with corresponding decreases in mRNA levels and nascent peptide degradation.
results.evaluation: Flow cytometry data clearly shows threefold and twofold decreases for NGD-CGA and NGD-AAA reporters respectively (C24-C25). Northern blots confirm mRNA level changes and show stabilization of 5' decay fragments in ski2Δ (C26). Western blots demonstrate nascent peptide degradation (C27). These data validate the reporter system used throughout the study.

results.result: Different sizes of ribosome-protected fragments (16, 21, and 28 nt RPFs) correspond to distinct ribosome states: 16 nt RPFs indicate ribosomes at truncated mRNA ends, 21 nt RPFs represent classical/decoding ribosomes, and 28 nt RPFs represent rotated/pre-translocation ribosomes.
results.evaluation: These interpretations of RPF sizes are well-supported by citations to previous work establishing these relationships (C53-C57). The use of ski2Δ backgrounds to stabilize truncated mRNAs (C58) is also supported by prior studies. This represents established methodology rather than a novel finding, but is critical for interpreting the ribosome profiling results.

results.result: The ubiquitin-binding domains of Cue2 may recognize Hel2-ubiquitinated sites on collided ribosomes to recruit the SMR domain, and may also regulate endonuclease activity.
results.evaluation: These claims are explicitly speculative (C86-C88) and lack direct experimental evidence. While the domain structure of Cue2 and the dependence on Hel2 are established, the specific mechanism of recruitment and regulation through ubiquitin-binding domains is not tested. This represents a reasonable hypothesis but requires further experimental validation.

results.result: Under conditions of cellular stress with overwhelming ribosome collisions, Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic processing may play an increased role, and the conservation of Cue2 suggests fundamental biological importance.
results.evaluation: The speculation about stress conditions (C91) is not directly tested in this study. While previous genetic screens show sensitivity of cue2Δ strains to ribosome-targeted compounds (C92), this is correlative. The inference about conservation (C93) is reasonable but not rigorously demonstrated. These represent plausible hypotheses requiring further investigation.

results.result: Slh1 and Dom34 may represent distinct ribosome rescue pathways targeting different substrates, with Slh1 acting on intact mRNAs and Dom34 on truncated mRNAs, and Cue2-mediated cleavage providing an alternative pathway for ribosome dissociation.
results.evaluation: While the ribosome profiling data shows increased occupancy in slh1Δ strains (C95) and increased Cue2 cleavage (C96), the proposed distinct specificities of Slh1 and Dom34 (C97-C98) are largely speculative. The role of Cue2 in providing an alternative dissociation pathway (C99) is inferred but not directly demonstrated. The model of two distinct rescue pathways (C101) is plausible but requires additional experimental validation.
